sections.title: Market Pulse: Indices Retreat Amid Rising Oil and Yields

items.headline: U.S. equities concluded Monday's session lower as a surge in oil prices, driven by renewed U.S.-Iran tensions, pushed bond yields higher and dampened investor sentiment. Defensive sectors showed resilience amidst broad market declines.
items.summary: The S&P 500, NASDAQ, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all finished in negative territory, reflecting heightened geopolitical risk and increasing borrowing costs. Despite the overall downturn, selected stocks demonstrated significant individual gains on company-specific news, while technology and consumer discretionary sectors faced considerable pressure. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Kodiak Sciences surges on positive Phase 3 trial results.
items.summary: Kodiak Sciences stock soared after its Zenkuda and tabirafusp-ted treatments met primary endpoints in a Phase 3 study for wet age-related macular degeneration.

items.headline: AMD joins trillion-dollar club on AI system advancements.
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) jumped as investors responded positively to its strategic pivot towards integrated AI systems and increased server market share, propelling it into the US$1 trillion market capitalization club.

items.headline: Bloom Energy leads S&P 500 gainers.
items.summary: Bloom Energy ($BE) was among the top performers in the S&P 500 today.

items.headline: MongoDB plummets following CEO's unexpected departure.
items.summary: MongoDB shares fell significantly after the announcement of its President and CEO's immediate departure.

items.headline: Roblox declines on analyst downgrade and bookings concerns.
items.summary: Roblox Corp. shares dropped after Jefferies downgraded the gaming company due to concerns about future bookings.

items.headline: Intel drops amid broader chip sector shifts.
items.summary: Intel Corporation shares fell, contributing to a broader dip among chip stocks.

items.headline: Consumer Staples Lead as Defensive Play; Tech and Discretionary Lag
items.summary: Consumer Staples emerged as the top-performing sector, gaining 0.4%, as investors sought defensive positions amidst rising Treasury yields and general market uncertainty. Conversely, Communication Services and Consumer Discretionary were the worst-performing sectors, falling 1.66% and 1.19% respectively.

items.headline: Rising Oil Prices and Bond Yields Pressure Equities
items.summary: Oil prices surged nearly 3%, with Brent crude trading above $100 per barrel, following President Trump's rejection of an Iranian truce offer, intensifying U.S.-Iran tensions. This pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.26% and the 30-year yield to 5.55%, making borrowing more expensive and hurting stock valuations.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Data Released, Fed Rate Hike Expectations Remain
items.summary: The University of Michigan reported that the final reading of the consumer sentiment index for September was 48.1%, slightly above estimates. However, both current economic conditions and consumer expectations sub-indices declined from August, while inflation expectations rose. Odds continue to favor a quarter-percentage point rate hike by the Federal Reserve next month.

items.headline: Companies Report Earnings; AI Investment Projections High
items.summary: Several companies, including GNS and NTWK, reported earnings before market open today, while IVA, JEF, MTN, IDT, and TRAK were scheduled to report after market close. Additionally, total investment in U.S. data centers and AI infrastructure is projected to reach $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032.
